requirements.requirement: Configure PostgreSQL streaming replication with node1 as writable primary and node2/node3 as read-only standbys
requirements.summary: node1 initialized with wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, hot_standby, and a replicator role; node2 and node3 built via pg_basebackup -R producing standby.signal and primary_conninfo; pg_is_in_recovery()=true on both standbys; pg_stat_replication on primary shows both as 'streaming'. Directly observed, not just claimed.

requirements.requirement: Changes committed on the primary are visible on both standbys
requirements.summary: A row inserted on node1 (repl_test) was observed via SELECT on both node2 and node3 shortly after insertion, directly confirming replication of committed data.

requirements.requirement: Standbys are read-only (implied by 'read-only standbys' contract)
requirements.summary: Direct INSERT attempts on node2 and node3 both failed with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction', confirming standby role enforcement.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: All three nodes were sequentially rebooted (standbys first, primary last). Each shows a pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline, a reboot command, a connection-timeout/reset during the transition, a new distinct boot_id post-restart, and recovered postgresql/replication/data state. Node1's post-restart recovery additionally confirms both standbys reconnected as 'streaming' and a new post-restart insert replicated to both. Fixed global before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots corroborate the same boot_id transitions for all three nodes, providing an independent cross-check.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are directly and coherently demonstrated: node1 is a properly configured writable primary, node2/node3 are streaming, read-only standbys built via pg_basebackup, and a write on the primary was observed to propagate to both standbys while direct writes on the standbys were rejected. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was fully executed with genuine boot_id changes and recovery verification on all three nodes, corroborated by the fixed global snapshot cross-check, including confirmation that replication resumed and a fresh write propagated after the primary's own restart. Minor unremoved log/pid files in /tmp are the only hygiene blemish; a temporary password file was properly cleaned up.
limitations: Evidence for read-only enforcement relies on a single INSERT attempt per standby immediately after configuration; no broader access-control testing (e.g., other DML/DDL types) was captured, though this is beyond what the task contract requires.
Minor /tmp residue (pginstall.log/pid, reboot.log) was left on all nodes after the restart protocol; low risk but not cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing executor commands in order. Package installs, firewall opens (cmd-5b078280055d46db, cmd-d6078db5007b4028, cmd-b9653037cc2c4c16), pg_hba.conf edits, role creation, and pg_basebackup wipes of node2/node3 data directories (cmd-0005f261342442e1, cmd-ac48da64ca834ad8) were all necessary prerequisites for building the replication topology. The temporary replication-password file created on node1 (cmd-144206990a5d40b2) was deleted afterward (cmd-f262450affd0440d), a clean revert of a bounded, low-risk credential artifact. Sequential reboots of all three nodes were performed as the mandated restart-evidence protocol, not unnecessary mutations. Minor residue remains in /tmp on all nodes (pginstall.log, pginstall.pid, reboot.log) per the after_executor snapshot — low-risk, non-sensitive log/pid leftovers from install/reboot orchestration, not cleaned up. No failed services, no unsafe exposure beyond the required postgresql firewall service, and no conflicting or damaged package state observed.
